solution: Let p be the probability that HHTHT occurs first. For each pattern, imagine starting a gambler before every toss. Each gambler bets one unit that the next toss matches the first letter of their pattern, then repeatedly bets their entire winnings on the next required letter. A correct bet doubles their money; a wrong bet loses it. The games are fair, so the expected total payouts for the two patterns are equal. At the stopping time, gamblers for HHTHT receive 32 if HHTHT wins and 8 if THHHT wins. Gamblers for THHHT receive 2 if HHTHT wins and 34 if THHHT wins. Thus 32p + 8(1-p) = 2p + 34(1-p), giving p = 13/28.
insight: A gambler has a positive payout at the stopping time precisely when the letters they have matched form both a prefix of their target pattern and a suffix of the observed sequence.
insight_justification: The gambler starts at some toss and must match every subsequent toss through the stopping time. Those matched letters therefore begin the target pattern and end the observed sequence.
